text:
**To:** Chair and Members of the Governing Body  
**From:** Head Teacher  
**Date:** [Date]  
**Re:** Staffing Budget Reduction – Options for 2024/25 (8% cut, class size cap 30)

---

### 1. Context and constraints

- **Budget reduction required:** 8% of the current staffing budget (approx. **£184,000** based on a £2.3m staffing budget).
- **Hard constraint:** No class may exceed **30 pupils** in any year group (statutory infant class size limit is 30; we will apply this as a school-wide cap for fairness and safety).
- **Current structure:** 400 pupils on roll, 14 classes (average 28.6 per class). Staffing includes: 14 class teachers, 1 full-time SENCo, 1 part-time music teacher (0.4 FTE), 1 full-time PE specialist (1.0 FTE), 6 teaching assistants (TAs) (total 4.2 FTE), 1 full-time HLTA, 1 part-time admin (0.6 FTE), 1 full-time family support worker.
- **Non-negotiable:** Safeguarding, statutory SEN provision, and teacher:pupil ratios for core subjects must remain compliant.

---

### 2. Options considered

#### Option A – Reduce teaching staff by 1.5 FTE (reorganise into mixed-year classes)

- **How:** Reduce from 14 classes to 13 classes. Merge Year 1/2 and Year 3/4 into two mixed-age classes. This releases 1.0 FTE teacher. Also reduce the PE specialist from 1.0 to 0.5 FTE (class teachers cover remaining PE).
- **Cost saving:** £72,000 (1.0 teacher) + £18,000 (0.5 PE) = **£90,000** (49% of target).
- **Damage:**
  - Mixed-age classes increase planning workload and may reduce attainment in Year 2 and Year 6 (SATs years) if not carefully managed.
  - PE curriculum quality drops; external competitions and after-school clubs reduced.
  - Class sizes rise to 30 in two classes (still legal, but less individual attention).
  - Parental concern about mixed-age teaching is high; likely complaints.
- **Remaining gap:** £94,000 still to find – would require further cuts to support staff (see Option D).

#### Option B – Reduce teaching assistant hours by 50% (from 4.2 FTE to 2.1 FTE)

- **How:** Keep all class teachers. Cut TA hours across all classes, focusing on removing 1:1 and small-group support in Years 3–6. Keep full TA support in Reception and Year 1 (early reading).
- **Cost saving:** 2.1 FTE × £22,000 average = **£46,200** (25% of target).
- **Damage:**
  - Significant loss of in-class support for SEND pupils (those with EHCPs will still get statutory hours, but those on SEN support will lose intervention).
  - Teachers will have to cover more administrative and pastoral tasks, reducing planning time.
  - Behaviour incidents likely to rise in upper KS2 without TA presence.
  - Pupil premium children (approx. 30% of school) will lose targeted catch-up support.
- **Remaining gap:** £137,800 – not viable alone.

#### Option C – Reduce non-class-based staff (SENCo, music, family support, admin)

- **How:** Make SENCo part-time (0.6 FTE) and share with another school; cut music teacher entirely; reduce family support worker to 0.5 FTE; reduce admin to 0.4 FTE.
- **Cost saving:** SENCo 0.4 FTE (£16,000) + music 0.4 FTE (£14,000) + family support 0.5 FTE (£12,000) + admin 0.2 FTE (£4,000) = **£46,000** (25% of target).
- **Damage:**
  - SENCo capacity halved – statutory SEN oversight at risk; EHCP annual reviews may be delayed.
  - Loss of music curriculum (no specialist) – reduces breadth and may affect school’s arts status.
  - Family support worker reduction increases safeguarding risk – more referrals to social care, more parental crises unmanaged.
  - Admin cut means head teacher and office staff will do more clerical work, reducing leadership time.
- **Remaining gap:** £138,000 – not viable alone.

#### Option D – Combination of A + B + C (the “full package”)

- **How:** Implement all three above simultaneously.
- **Cost saving:** £90,000 + £46,200 + £46,000 = **£182,200** (99% of target – round up with minor supply savings to hit £184,000).
- **Damage (cumulative):**
  - **Teaching quality:** Mixed-age classes in two year groups; PE specialist halved; music gone.
  - **SEND support:** TA hours halved; SENCo part-time – children with mild/moderate needs will regress; more exclusions likely.
  - **Safeguarding:** Family support worker cut by half – increased risk of missed early help.
  - **Staff morale:** Redundancies across all roles; remaining staff face heavier workloads; likely resignations.
  - **Parental trust:** Significant negative reaction; possible pupil movement to other schools.
  - **Curriculum:** Loss of arts and PE breadth; core subjects still covered but with less differentiation.
- **Remaining gap:** £1,800 – can be found by reducing supply budget and CPD.

---

### 3. Recommendation

**I do not recommend any single option as a standalone solution** – none meets the 8% target without severe damage. However, **Option D is the only realistic way to meet the full £184,000 cut** while keeping class sizes at or below 30.

**My recommendation is a modified Option D, phased over two years, with mitigations:**

1. **Year 1 (2024/25):** Implement Option A (mixed-year classes + PE reduction) and Option C (non-class staff cuts) – saving £136,000. Do **not** cut TA hours yet.
2. **Year 2 (2025/26):** If the budget position does not improve, implement a **smaller TA cut (1.0 FTE, not 2.1)** – saving £22,000 – and find the remaining £26,000 through non-staff budgets (energy, supplies, voluntary contributions).

**Why this is better:**
- Protects early years and SEND support for one more year.
- Gives time to consult parents and staff on mixed-age classes.
- Allows natural turnover (retirements, resignations) to reduce redundancy costs.
- Keeps the school legally compliant and safe.

**However, I must be transparent:** even this phased approach will damage educational quality and staff wellbeing. The governing body should formally write to the local authority and parents explaining that an 8% staffing cut without raising class sizes is **not sustainable** without harming children’s outcomes. I recommend we also explore:
- Applying for a **financial hardship grant** from the DfE.
- Seeking **shared services** (business manager, SENCo) with a neighbouring school.
- Launching a **parental fundraising campaign** to fund one TA post.

**Decision required:** The governing body must choose between:
- (a) Accepting the full Option D package now (fastest, most damaging),
- (b) Accepting my phased recommendation (slower, less damaging),
- (c) Rejecting the cut and asking the LA for a revised budget (risking legal non-compliance).

I urge you to choose **(b)** and to support my request for a formal appeal against the budget settlement.
